The market gap
A $2.8B category with no winner in the SMB tier
Oracle, SAP, E2open dominate enterprise. HubSpot, Salesforce serve SaaS. The 250,000+ SMB trading companies — the actual engine of world trade — have no category-native software. That's the gap Setu Flow is built to own.
The moat
Trade logic is hard to replicate in a generic tool
FX calculations, freight basis selection, margin approval gates, country compliance checklists, and dual buyer/supplier pipelines — each is a feature that a generic CRM cannot add via a plugin. Setu Flow is native to this workflow. The first 9 modules are shipped and live.
The timing
Post-COVID trade digitization is half-done, and India is at $1T
Trade teams moved off paper in 2020. They landed on general CRMs that don't fit. Now they're actively switching — and India's $1T export target is funneling policy support and demand into the exact SMB exporter segment Setu Flow serves.
The problem

International trade teams are drowning in manual commercial work.

A 30-person food export company receives 80 inbound inquiries a week from trade shows, emails, referrals, and WhatsApp. They close maybe 12. The gap isn't demand — it's how long it takes to qualify, quote, and follow up.

  • 01

    Contacts captured on business cards that never enter a system

    Trade show leads written on paper, photographed, then emailed to someone who may or may not enter them. 40–60% are never followed up within 72 hours — the critical window.

  • 02

    Quoting done in Excel with no freight, FX, or approval logic

    Sales teams manually calculate FOB vs. CIF pricing, convert currencies, estimate freight, and email a PDF — every time, from scratch. No version control, no audit trail, no manager visibility.

  • 03

    No visibility into pipeline until it's already lost

    Management gets a weekly status call. By the time overdue follow-ups are visible, the buyer has moved on. CRMs show a contact list — they don't show which deal needs action today.

  • 04

    Compliance and document checklists managed in email threads

    Phytosanitary certificates, country-specific import regulations, LC requirements — tracked across email chains, WhatsApp groups, and shared folders with no system of record.

Market opportunity

A $2.8B category growing 10–12% a year, with no clear winner for SMB exporters.

The global trade management software market is dominated by enterprise vendors built for Fortune 500 logistics teams — Oracle, SAP, E2open, Descartes. Minimum viable contract: $50,000 and 6 months of implementation.

The 50–500-person import-export operator — the engine of world trade — is left to Excel, email, and general CRMs that don't understand freight, FX, or how commercial trade actually works.

That's the gap Setu Flow is built to own.

Why now

Three macro forces converging — the window to build the dominant trade OS is open right now.

2024–2025

Post-COVID trade digitization is real — but half-done

COVID forced global trade teams off spreadsheets onto whatever SaaS tools were available. They adopted general CRMs that handled contacts but not trade logic. Now they're stuck with tools that don't fit — and actively looking for category-specific alternatives.

Source · McKinsey Global Trade Report 2024
2024–2030

India's $1T export mission needs faster quoting, not more demand

The Government of India's $1T exports-by-2030 target is funneling policy support, credit lines, and trade-show subsidies to mid-market exporters. The bottleneck isn't demand — it's how slowly small teams can qualify, quote, and convert buyer inquiries into confirmed orders.

Source · Ministry of Commerce, GoI 2024 directive
2025

Assistive AI + operator approval is the enterprise-ready pattern

Generic AI agents make headlines but break inside regulated, multi-party workflows like trade. The winning pattern — assistive AI + locked operator approval + audit trail — is exactly what enterprise buyers are demanding. Setu Flow was built for this from day one. Our AI suggestions queue drafts, operators approve, every action is logged.

Source · Anthropic enterprise reports 2025
The category insight

Generic CRMs sell pipelines.
Trade teams need execution.

Salesforce, HubSpot, and Zoho were built for SaaS sales — predictable products, fixed pricing, domestic delivery. None of those assumptions hold for international trade. Enterprise tools (SAP, E2open) solve it — but cost $50k+ to implement and take 6 months. We sit exactly in the gap.

Live product

One locked flow. Every step connected.

Setu Flow isn't a collection of disconnected modules — it's a single commercial operating flow where each step feeds the next, with full visibility at every stage.

setuflow.com/contact-exchange/vcard

Smart capture — any touchpoint, instant lead

At a trade show, a conference, or from an inbound email — every contact becomes a qualified lead with inherited context before the salesperson leaves the booth.

1My Card (outward) — your branded digital card with QR code and public capture form. Buyers scan and submit — you get a lead instantly.
2vCard / OCR capture — scan a business card or import a vCard. Contact details + trade event source auto-populated into a new lead.
3Trade-show batch entry — end of day, enter 20 contacts from a show. Each one inherits the event name, date, and booth as source context.
4AI suggestions queue — AI drafts follow-up suggestions for new leads. Operator reviews and approves — nothing auto-sends.

Business model

Simple SaaS pricing. Built to scale with the team.

Per-seat monthly SaaS with an annual discount. No implementation fees. No per-quote charges. The pricing model is designed so a 10-person team can start immediately, and a 200-person enterprise unlocks volume pricing and SSO.

The wedge is design partners at introductory pricing — 10 confirmed at $400–800/mo — converting to standard pricing post-design-partner phase.
